papers.title: Property-driven State-Space Coarsening for Continuous Time Markov Chains
papers.abstract: Dynamical systems with large state-spaces are often expensive to thoroughly explore experimentally. Coarse-graining methods aim to define simpler systems which are more amenable to analysis and exploration; most current methods, however, focus on a priori state aggregation based on similarities in transition rates, which is not necessarily reflected in similar behaviours at the level of trajectories. We propose a way to coarsen the state-space of a system which optimally preserves the satisfaction of a set of logical specifications about the system's trajectories. Our approach is based on Gaussian Process emulation and Multi-Dimensional Scaling, a dimensionality reduction technique which optimally preserves distances in non-Euclidean spaces. We show how to obtain low-dimensional visualisations of the system's state-space from the perspective of properties' satisfaction, and how to define macro-states which behave coherently with respect to the specifications. Our approach is illustrated on a non-trivial running example, showing promising performance and high computational efficiency.

summary_zh.motivation: 降低大状态空间系统的探索成本
summary_zh.method: 使用高斯过程仿真和多维缩放进行状态空间粗粒化

summary_zh.validation: 在一个非平凡示例上验证

summary_en.motivation: To reduce the computational cost of exploring dynamical systems with large state-spaces by coarsening while preserving behavior relevant to logical specifications.
summary_en.method: Combines Gaussian Process emulation with Multi-Dimensional Scaling to achieve dimensionality reduction that optimally preserves property satisfaction.
summary_en.result: Produces low-dimensional visualizations and coherent macro-states with high computational efficiency.
summary_en.validation: Demonstrated on a non-trivial continuous-time Markov chain example.

papers.title: Oxides, porosity and fatigue performance of AlSi10Mg parts produced by selective laser melting
papers.first_author_affiliation: Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, PA, USA

corresponding_authors.name: Petrus Christiaan Pistorius
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, PA, USA

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究AlSi10Mg铝合金的SLM工艺与疲劳性能，与生物医学植入物方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper uses a non-biocompatible aluminum alloy (AlSi10Mg) and does not address implant-related stress shielding, stiffness matching, osseointegration, or any biomedical application.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究SLM成型AlSi10Mg的氧化物和孔隙对疲劳性能的影响
summary_zh.method: 通过调控激光参数改变孔隙率和氧化物分布并进行疲劳测试
summary_zh.result: 氧化物和孔隙显著影响疲劳寿命，高孔隙率降低疲劳强度
summary_zh.validation: 与常规铸态AlSi10Mg疲劳性能对比验证

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of oxides and porosity on the fatigue performance of AlSi10Mg parts fabricated by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Varied laser parameters to control porosity and oxide formation, followed by fatigue testing.
summary_en.result: Oxides and porosity significantly degrade fatigue life, with higher porosity leading to reduced fatigue strength.
summary_en.validation: Validated by comparison with conventionally cast AlSi10Mg fatigue data.

papers.title: Proximal Femur Bone Density Decreases up to 5 Years After Total Hip Arthroplasty in Young, Active Patients

corresponding_authors.name: Denis Nam
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Department of Orthopedic Surgery, Washington University School of Medicine/Barnes-Jewish Hospital, St. Louis, Missouri

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文仅提供临床骨密度数据，未涉及植入物力学分析或有限元建模。
llm.why_not_core: No finite element modeling, no implant contact mechanics, no quantification of stress shielding or micromotion.

summary_zh.motivation: 年轻全髋置换患者术后股骨近端骨密度长期变化未知
summary_zh.method: 对年轻患者术后五年内定期进行双能X线吸收测量
summary_zh.result: 术后五年内股骨近端骨密度持续下降

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate long-term periprosthetic bone mineral density changes in young, active patients after total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: Prospective DEXA follow-up over 5 years in young patients.
summary_en.result: Proximal femur bone density decreased significantly up to 5 years postoperatively.
summary_en.validation: Clinical DEXA measurements in a patient cohort.

papers.title: Granular gel support-enabled extrusion of three-dimensional alginate and cellular structures.
papers.abstract: Freeform fabrication of soft structures has been of great interest in recent years. In particular, it is viewed as a critical step toward the grand vision of organ printing--the on-demand design and fabrication of three-dimensional (3D) human organ constructs for implantation and regenerative medicine. The objective of this study is to develop a novel granular gel support material-enabled, two-step gelation-based 'printing-then-gelation' approach to fabricate 3D alginate structures using filament extrusion. Specifically, a granular Carbopol microgel bath holds the ungelled alginate structure being extruded, avoiding the instantaneous gelation of each printed layer as well as resultant surface tension-induced nozzle clogging. Since Carbopol microgels react with multivalent cations, which are needed for alginate crosslinking, gelatin is introduced as a sacrificial material to make an alginate and gelatin bioink for extrusion, which gels thermally (step-one gelation) to initially stabilize the printed structure for removal from Carbopol. Then gelatin is melted and diffused away while alginate is ionically crosslinked in a 37 °C calcium chloride bath (step-two gelation), resulting in an alginate structure. The proposed 'printing-then-gelation' approach works for alginate structure fabrication, and it is also applicable for the printing of cellular constructs and other similar homogeneous soft structures using a two-step or even multi-step approach. The main conclusions are: (1) 0.8% (w/v) Carbopol bath with a neutral pH value may be most suitable for soft structure printing; (2) it is most effective to use a 0.9% (w/v) NaCl solution to facilitate the removal of residual Carbopol; and (3) alginate structures fabricated using the proposed approach demonstrate better mechanical properties than those fabricated using the conventional 'gelation-while-printing' approach.
papers.first_author_affiliation: Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, University of Florida, Gainesville, FL 32611, USA.

summary_en.motivation: To develop a support material enabling freeform fabrication of soft hydrogel structures.
summary_en.method: A granular Carbopol microgel bath combined with a two-step gelation using alginate/gelatin bioink.
summary_en.result: The approach successfully prints 3D alginate structures with improved mechanical properties compared to conventional gelation-while-printing.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing comparing Carbopol concentration and NaCl rinsing.
